figures.question: Are corresponding local tick shifts reproducible under mesh, time and box controls?
figures.reading: Every base preparation has 6 baseline ticks available for pairing. Largest base tick shift 5.32e-07 cycles; largest predicted tick-shift error 8.42e-09 cycles.
figures.significance: The measured response reaches an identifiable local clock record, with numerical sensitivity displayed independently.
figures.limitation: Tick ordinals are anchored to the common preparation in one flat frame. Physical emission/reception marker invariance and two-object recoil are still untested. Values below 1e-16 are plotted at that floor.
transformations: linearly interpolate positive-going local zeros; delta_N=-Omega*delta_t/(2*pi); ordinal pairing; direct grid/time/box differences

figures.question: Is the clock difference even in packet sign and quadratic in amplitude?
figures.reading: Weak amplitude exponent 1.9993540; normalized ladder difference 0.00728; sign-odd/even norm ratio 0.
figures.significance: The amplitude ladder discriminates second-order forcing from a linear response, while sign parity checks the exact action symmetry.
figures.limitation: Exact numerical sign parity is strongly enforced by this deterministic action. It alone does not validate the magnitude or operational meaning of the clock response.
transformations: divide matched difference by A squared; compute half-sum and half-difference of +/-A responses; no fitted curves

figures.question: Does the precomputed second-order response predict the local clock difference?
figures.reading: Base relative L2 prediction error is 0.00194 for one packet and 0.00193 for counterpropagating shells. Prediction files were locked before receiver runs.
figures.significance: Agreement tests the derived neutral-to-core-to-clock response coefficient, beyond the symmetry-enforced sign parity.
figures.limitation: The Taylor predictor and nonlinear solver share the discrete Hamiltonian; independent Hamiltonian and Taylor checks plus numerical refinements constrain, but do not eliminate, shared implementation error.
transformations: matched no-pulse subtraction at the same radius and time; subtract saved A² prediction; no fitting

figures.question: What neutral waveform actually reaches the upstream recording sphere?
figures.reading: The saved trace includes both initial passage and later returning radiation. Dividing by signed A overlays the weak single-packet waveforms.
figures.significance: Reception is compared against a recorded input field, with compact preparations and sign controls available for audit.
figures.limitation: A single scalar waveform does not separate incoming/outgoing characteristics; this run predicts from full registered initial data, not waveform-only inversion.
transformations: select base grid cases 1-5; divide each waveform by its signed input coefficient

figures.question: Where do the compact neutral packets travel relative to the clock core?
figures.reading: Saved radial neutral-field histories show incoming propagation, central reflection and the separately prepared outgoing control. The upstream sphere is r=14.
figures.significance: This locates the forcing in space and time and makes the concentric-shell geometry explicit.
figures.limitation: Spherical focusing is physical in this restricted preparation; it is not an opposing-beam or recoil experiment. Color scales are independent.
transformations: reshape saved t,r rows into heatmaps; independent symmetric color scales; approximate core band 0<r<10
